messages.subject: Random number streams
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am looking for a functionality that would be very useful for the simulation model I am implementing. In particular, I should use a different stream of random numbers for each probability distribution used in the model similarly to what happens in Arena Simulation Software, where one can fix a seed for each probability distribution after specifying its parameters. 

In my case fixing the seed at the beginning of the simulation is not enough. For instance, suppose that the seed is fixed and that my simulation consists of only two activities, independent of each other (they are associated to separate generators and separate resources), whose durations are generated from two different probability distributions. If I change the parameters of one probability distribution, events may show up within the Simmer schedule in a different order than before and this may cause the probability distribution with unchanged parameters to return different values. Instead, I would like the values generated from the probability distribution with unchanged parameters to be the same as before. If you could suggest a way to implement what I need, I would be very grateful.

Thank you very much for your time.  

Tommaso

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Random number streams
parts:
Hi Tommaso,

The fact that sampling is decoupled from the DES engine gives you full
flexibility. A simple wrapper can set and restore a seed:

fix_seed <- function(seed, rfun, ...) {
args <- list(...)
set.seed(seed)
save.seed <- get(".Random.seed", .GlobalEnv)
function() {
assign(".Random.seed", save.seed, .GlobalEnv)
out <- do.call(rfun, args)
save.seed <<- get(".Random.seed", .GlobalEnv)
out
}
}

Then,

exp_gen <- fix_seed(42, rexp, 1, 1)
norm_gen <- fix_seed(13, rnorm, 1, 5)

etc.

Iñaki
